title: Four ways to name a genetic variant

segs.text: Section one. Naming genetic variants. The same genetic variant can be written four ways, depending on which system the scientists who first described it chose. Papers, guidance documents and genotype reports use all four, so a pharmacist has to read each one and know what each one tells you: where in the gene the change is, which version is the wild type, meaning the normal version, and which is the variant. One more rule applies to every gene: the gene symbol is written in italics and the protein is not. So T P M T in italics is the gene, and T P M T in plain type is the enzyme, thiopurine methyltransferase.

The first system is allele numeric or alphabetic nomenclature. V K O R C one, eleven seventy three C, and V K O R C one, eleven seventy three T, name two versions of the same spot. You get the gene symbol, the position of the nucleotide, meaning the D N A base, counted from the start codon where the gene's protein code begins, and the base found there. You do not get which one is the wild type. Only a writer who follows the convention, wild type in a capital letter and the variant in lowercase, tells you that.

The S N P system, for single nucleotide polymorphism, fixes that. V K O R C one, eleven seventy three, C to T, gives the gene, the position, the wild type nucleotide first, an arrow, and then the variant. A second example is A B C B one, thirty four thirty five, C to T. A B C B one is the gene for P-glycoprotein. The trap is reading the order backward. In C to T, C is the wild type, because the wild type is always written first.

The star system writes the gene, then a star and a number for the allele. She said, We always call star one for whatever gene we're talking about, that's the wild type version. The name does not say where the change is or what it is, so you need a table that defines each star allele. Star numbers follow the order of discovery, not position. C Y P two C nineteen star two, six eighty one G to A, was characterized first. Star three, six thirty six G to A, was found later, yet lies closer to the start codon. And each lab numbers its own gene's variants, so C Y P two C nine star two is not at six eighty one.

The reference S N P system, or r s, gives each S N P a number from the S N P database, d b S N P, that no other S N P has. The Human Genome Variation Society recommends it as the standard. C Y P two C nineteen star three, which is C Y P two C nineteen six thirty six G to A, is r s four nine eight, six eight nine three. The number names one S N P and nothing more. To learn the gene, the position or the wild type, you must search a database that is hard to query. So of the four systems, r s is the one that does not easily tell you which allele is the wild type.
